title: Abu Dhabi Pitches Two, Four and Seven-Day Diwali Getaways
excerpt: DCT Abu Dhabi has published Diwali itineraries built around Yas Island, Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, Saadiyat and the desert — a three-to-four-hour flight from major Indian cities, with prices and offers left to its official campaign page.
body:
• The Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi (DCT Abu Dhabi) has published Diwali itineraries of two, four and seven days, built around Yas Island theme parks, Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, the Saadiyat Cultural District and trips beyond the city.
  • Abu Dhabi is a three-to-four-hour flight from major Indian cities, according to DCT Abu Dhabi, making a two-day Yas Island break the short option and a week the full family version.
  • The announcement is an itinerary guide, not a fare sale: it gives no package prices. Planning, hotel deals and dining offers sit on the official Visit Abu Dhabi Diwali campaign page.
  • For diaspora readers in the US weighing a Diwali trip, this is a Gulf stopover-length option aimed at Indian travellers — check visa and partner-offer terms on the campaign page before booking.

What DCT Abu Dhabi has published

The Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi is highlighting a set of travel experiences for the Diwali holidays, with options spanning short weekend breaks and weeklong family getaways, according to its announcement carried by Travel Daily Media and the original release on PR Newswire. The pitch is aimed at Indian travellers: Abu Dhabi is, in the department's words, only a three-to-four-hour flight from major Indian cities, close enough for a long weekend and large enough to fill a full week.

Two days: Yas Island

The shortest itinerary stays on Yas Island. Day one pairs the rides and slides at Yas Waterworld Abu Dhabi with festive shopping at Yas Mall, ending with sunset at Yas Bay Waterfront. Day two is built around speed, sea life and sand: the rollercoasters at Ferrari World Abu Dhabi, an afternoon at SeaWorld Abu Dhabi, and time on Yas Beach. For a family taking only the Diwali weekend, that is the whole trip — theme parks, shopping and waterfront dining without crossing the city.

Four days: add the mosque, the palace and Saadiyat

The four-day version keeps the two Yas Island days and adds the emirate's cultural circuit. Day three, in the release's outline, starts with a morning at Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, moves to Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental Abu Dhabi, and takes in sunset views from Observation Deck at 300. The final day heads to Saadiyat Island — the Saadiyat Cultural District and the Mamsha Al Saadiyat beachfront promenade, with the Natural History Museum and Zayed National Museum named as stops, and dinner by the water.

Seven days: desert, Al Ain and the mangroves

The weeklong itinerary covers the Yas Island and Saadiyat stops first, then heads beyond the city in its second half. Day five is the desert: Al Wathba Fossil Dunes Reserve, a desert safari and overnight camping. Day six goes to the Al Ain region, including the UNESCO-listed Al Ain Oasis and Al Ain Adventure Park. Day seven winds down with the mangroves of Jubail Mangrove Park, shopping at The Galleria Al Maryah Island, and an evening walk along the Corniche.

Before you book: what the announcement does not do

Read the announcement for what it is. It names itineraries and attractions; it does not publish prices, flight schedules or bookable packages, and neither source in this article attaches a fare to any of the three options. The place to check current terms is the official campaign page: Visit Abu Dhabi's Diwali page carries Diwali hotel deals and special dining offers, and advertises a partner promotion for a free visa running to November 15 — the page's own wording ties that offer to bookings through its partners, so check the partner terms there before relying on it. Entry requirements and any offer can change, and the campaign page, not a press release, is the live source.

For Indian-diaspora families, the realistic use of this announcement is as a shortlist: two days if Diwali is a weekend trip, four if the mosque and museums matter as much as the theme parks, and seven only if the desert and Al Ain are part of the plan. Everything beyond that — price, visa and availability — has to be verified on the official page at booking time.
